titulo: Using the imperative with reflexive pronouns: affirmative commands
subtitulo: ¡Levántate! ¡Siéntese! ¡Vámonos! The pronoun hooks onto the end of the command.
regla: In affirmative commands with reflexive verbs, the pronoun goes after the verb, attached to it. With nosotros, the final s drops: levantémonos.

bloques.texto: When you give a **positive** command with a **reflexive verb** (**levantarse**, **sentarse**, **ponerse**, **irse**...), the pronoun always goes **after** the verb and is **attached** to it, as one word.
**Nosotros** has one extra rule: the **-mos** ending loses its **s** before **nos**. **Levantemos** + **nos** → **levantémonos**, never **levantémosnos**.

Adding a syllable leaves the stress where it was, but now it sits further from the end, so a **written accent** appears to keep the sound: **levanta** → **levántate**, **siente** → **siéntese**, **vayan** → **váyanse**. One-syllable commands like **pon** or **ve** don't need it: **ponte**, **vete**.
Tip: the pronoun is a backpack. In a positive command, you carry it on your back, stuck to the verb: **¡Siéntate!**

lista.es: ¡==Ponte== el traje, el agua está helada!
lista.en: Put your wetsuit on, the water is freezing! (tú)
Get up now, there are waves! (tú)

lista.es: ==Siéntese== aquí, por favor; ahorita le abro el carro.
lista.en: Sit down here, please; I'll open your car right away. (usted)

lista.es: ¡==Lávense== las manos antes de los tacos!
lista.en: Wash your hands before the tacos! (ustedes)
Let's get up early to surf!

lista.nota: In a positive command the pronoun never goes in front.
Keep the stress where it was: written accent.
You'll hear **siéntensen** in casual speech, but the standard form has only one **n**, before **se**.
